draft.title: The Long March
card: By 1934 the Nationalist government under Jiang Jieshi had surrounded the Communists' base in Jiangxi in south-east China. Nationalist forces were closing in, and staying put risked destruction.
In October 1934 the Red Army broke out and retreated. Over about a year it marched thousands of kilometres through mountains, rivers and grasslands to the north-west, ending in Shaanxi in late 1935.
The march was costly. Most of the people who set out did not arrive, because of fighting, hunger, cold and illness.
At a meeting at Zunyi in January 1935, party leaders accepted Mao Zedong as the main leader of the army. The march saved the Communists as a force, and Mao's authority in the party grew from it.
draft.remember: The Long March was a retreat that saved the Communists and made Mao their leader.

a.q: Why did the Communists begin the Long March in 1934?
opts: Nationalist forces had surrounded their Jiangxi base
They had defeated the Nationalists and were moving north
Japan had invaded and forced them out of their base
They wanted to spread communism to the cities of the coast
a.why: The Nationalists had closed in on the Jiangxi base, so the Communists broke out to survive. It was a retreat, not an advance after a victory, so the option about defeating the Nationalists is wrong.
a.clue: Think about whether the Communists were attacking or in danger.

b.q: A student says the Long March was a failure because most marchers did not survive. Which reply best uses the card?
opts: It kept the Communists alive as a force and lifted Mao
It ended with the capture of Jiang Jieshi in Shaanxi
It won Communist control of the cities of eastern China
It showed the Communists had dropped their revolution
b.why: Despite heavy losses, the march let the Communists escape destruction and reach a new base, and Mao emerged as the main leader. The losses were real, but they do not make it a failure in outcome. Jiang Jieshi was not captured, and the march was a retreat, not a conquest of cities.
b.clue: Ask what the Communists had at the end that they might have lost.

a.best: Nationalist forces had surrounded their Jiangxi base

b.best: It kept the Communists alive as a force and lifted Mao

problems.detail: The why says flatly that 'Jiang Jieshi was not captured', but Jiang was captured in December 1936 at Xi'an, Shaanxi, by Zhang Xueliang (the Xi'an Incident). This was not the end of the march and not the Communists' doing, but Year 12 students who know the Xi'an Incident may be confused. The distractor 'capture of Jiang Jieshi in Shaanxi' is also close to a real event. Reword the why to say the march did not end with Jiang's capture, or use a different distractor.
